events.title: Li Shimin destroys Xue Rengao's army at Qianshuiyuan
events.description: Li Shimin, the future Emperor Taizong of Tang, waited until the supplies of the Qin state ran short and then destroyed Xue Rengao's army at Qianshuiyuan, in present-day Shaanxi. Xue Rengao surrendered and was executed, opening the north-west to the Tang.

events.title: The Abbasids defeat the Qarmatians at the Battle of Hama
events.description: An Abbasid army under Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Katib defeated pro-Isma'ili Bedouin near Hama in Syria, capturing and executing their leaders. The victory made possible the Abbasid reconquest of the Tulunid domains in southern Syria and Egypt.

events.title: A great earthquake strikes Marash and the crusader lands
events.description: An earthquake with an estimated magnitude of 7.4 to 7.7 struck the area of Marash, now Kahramanmaraş, and also hit Antioch, Mamistra and Edessa in the crusader lands. At least 40,000 people were killed, a figure historians contest.

events.title: Cardinal Wolsey dies on his way to face treason charges
events.description: Thomas Wolsey, once Henry VIII's all-powerful Lord Chancellor, died at Leicester Abbey. He had fallen from favour after failing to obtain the annulment of Henry's marriage to Catherine of Aragon.

events.title: English East India Company ships defeat the Portuguese off Swally
events.description: The naval Battle of Swally, fought on 29 and 30 November off Suvali near Surat, ended in victory for four English East India Company galleons over four Portuguese galleons and 26 barks. It loosened the Portuguese Empire's hold on India.

events.title: British reinforcements end the Patriot siege of Fort Cumberland
events.description: British reinforcements ended a siege of Fort Cumberland by Patriot militia under Jonathan Eddy. With four to five hundred volunteers and Natives and little support from Massachusetts, Eddy had tried to bring the American Revolutionary War to Nova Scotia.

events.title: Colorado troops massacre Cheyenne and Arapaho at Sand Creek
events.description: Colonel John Chivington's volunteer cavalry attacked a peaceful camp at Sand Creek, Colorado, killing about 150 to 200 people, mostly women, children and the elderly. Congressional inquiries condemned the attack.

events.title: The UN votes to partition Palestine
events.description: The UN General Assembly adopted Resolution 181, recommending separate Jewish and Arab states with Jerusalem under international control. Fighting broke out the next day.

events.title: Johnson sets up the Warren Commission
events.description: President Lyndon Johnson appointed a commission under Chief Justice Earl Warren to investigate Kennedy's assassination. Its 1964 report concluded that Lee Harvey Oswald acted alone.

song: fur-trading voyageurs and river boatmen of the Missouri and Mississippi; later deep-sea sailors
A song of the river traders and sailors of the 1800s, who sang it while hauling in a ship's anchor.
